scope: Primary-source support for the representative Chapter 3 distinction among working context, context window, conversation state, product memory, retrieval and training. This packet bounds claims; it does not supply or approve chapter prose.

claims.ruledClaim: A context window is the bounded amount of tokenised material a model can reference while producing a particular response. Exact capacity and which inputs count are model- and product-specific and must be rechecked.

sources.title: Machine Learning Glossary — context window
sources.support: Defines a context window in tokens and connects larger windows to the information usable for a response.
sources.scopeLimit: A glossary-level definition; it does not specify the exact contents or capacity of any LAiDIES reader's product.

sources.title: Context windows — Claude Platform Docs
sources.support: Distinguishes a model's working context from its training corpus and lists messages, tool results, images, documents and tool definitions as possible request material in Claude's API.
sources.scopeLimit: Claude-specific implementation detail; use only as a concrete example, never as a universal product rule.

claims.freshnessTrigger: Any change to the cited definitions, the representative product examples or a claim about a particular model's context capacity or contents.

claims.ruledClaim: Inference uses an already trained model to produce a response from current input. Training is a different process. Whether user data may later be retained or used for model improvement is a separate provider, product, plan and settings question.

sources.title: Machine Learning Glossary — inference
sources.support: Defines LLM inference as using a trained model to generate a response to an input prompt.
sources.scopeLimit: Supports the training-versus-use distinction, not a provider's data-retention or model-improvement policy.

sources.title: Conversation state — OpenAI API
sources.support: Separately documents API response retention and OpenAI's consent boundary for using API data to train models.
sources.scopeLimit: OpenAI API-specific and time-sensitive; it does not establish the policy for ChatGPT or another provider.

claims.freshnessTrigger: Before prose self-review and release, and whenever a provider, plan, privacy setting or data-use policy is named.

claims.ruledClaim: Conversation continuity is managed by the surrounding product or API. A system can pass prior turns or link stored response state into a later request; a smooth conversation therefore does not prove one human-like memory or that every visible earlier detail reached the model this time.

sources.title: Conversation state — OpenAI API
sources.locator: OpenAI APIs for conversation state; previous_response_id
sources.support: Shows both manually managed conversation state and stateful continuation using a previous response identifier.
sources.scopeLimit: One provider's API design. The chapter must describe the general surrounding-system role and label this as an example.

claims.freshnessTrigger: Any change to the API guide or any claim that a named chat product always includes, stores or exposes a particular prior turn.

claims.ruledClaim: Product memory is a product feature, not a synonym for the model's context window or training. A product may retain selected information separately from chat history and may use it in later response context; controls and behaviour vary by product and can change.

sources.title: Memory FAQ
sources.locator: How does saved memories work?; How long does ChatGPT keep saved memories?
sources.support: Describes saved memories as details used in response context and stored separately from chat history in ChatGPT.
sources.scopeLimit: ChatGPT-specific, account- and rollout-sensitive. It must not be generalized to every AI product.

claims.freshnessTrigger: Before prose self-review and release, and whenever ChatGPT memory controls or retention behaviour are described.

claims.ruledClaim: Retrieval can fetch information after training and supply it to a model for a response. Retrieval can improve grounding, but the source may still be stale, incomplete, irrelevant or outside the user's permission, so retrieval does not itself prove truth or authority.

sources.title: Machine Learning Glossary — grounding and retrieval-augmented generation
sources.support: Defines grounding as basing a response on retrieved sources and RAG as giving a trained LLM access to retrieved knowledge.
sources.scopeLimit: The source supports the mechanism and intended benefit. The chapter must independently retain the limits on source quality, scope and permission.

claims.freshnessTrigger: Any change to the mechanism claim, any named retrieval product or source, or any assertion that retrieval guarantees accuracy.

teachingBoundary.chapterOwns: The diagnostic distinction among what is visible, stored, retrievable and actually supplied to the model for this run.
teachingBoundary.chapterDoesNotOwn: A complete treatment of grounding, tools, APIs or product wrappers; Chapter 4 and Chapter 6 retain those durable jobs.
teachingBoundary.providerBoundary: Provider documentation supplies bounded examples. No provider-specific behaviour becomes a universal fact.
teachingBoundary.releaseRule: Recheck every current provider statement and every model-specific quantity before exact-prose self-review and again before release.
